coverage.selection: 22 individually reviewed primary publications; a curated selection rather than an exhaustive incident database.
coverage.date_policy: The selected history uses publication dates for its window and chronology. Event dates, where an exact incident day is established, remain separate. Null event dates mean no exact day is asserted.
limitations: Coverage is uneven despite a selected publication in each calendar-month bucket; absence of an entry never means absence of incidents.
Some in-window disclosures describe campaigns that began before the window; summaries identify this explicitly.
Dates and findings reflect the primary pages reviewed on the curation date; publisher corrections and updates may change later.
The separate CISA KEV collection uses catalog-addition dates, not incident or disclosure dates.
Source research, advisories and first-party incident disclosures carry different evidence; none establishes exposure of the reader's devices.

entries.title: CERT-EU warns of WSUS remote code execution
entries.summary: CERT-EU describes CVE-2025-59287, an unauthenticated code-execution flaw affecting Windows Server with the WSUS role enabled. Review the vendor's affected-product and update guidance; a Windows installation alone does not establish applicability.

entries.title: GTIG documents AI-enabled malware and threat-actor tool use
entries.summary: Google reports both experimental and operational AI-enabled malware, including runtime model calls and abuse of developer AI tools. Distinguish observed activity from prototypes; review model-API egress and the privileges held by local AI tooling.

entries.title: Anthropic discloses an AI-orchestrated espionage campaign
entries.summary: Anthropic reports a campaign detected in September 2025 that abused Claude Code against selected organizations. Attribution and automation estimates are the provider's assessments. This November disclosure does not date the start of activity to the history window.

entries.title: GitLab identifies a renewed Shai-Hulud npm campaign
entries.summary: GitLab researchers describe infected npm packages that steal developer and cloud credentials, propagate through publishing access and include destructive behavior. Review dependency histories and credential exposure; package counts in this ongoing report are not a complete victim inventory.

entries.title: React discloses remote code execution in Server Components
entries.summary: The React team discloses CVE-2025-55182 in React Server Components payload decoding. Review affected server packages and the latest vendor patch guidance. Client-only React applications without the relevant server integration are outside the described scope.

entries.title: FBI updates warning on AI-voice impersonation of officials
entries.summary: The FBI updates a continuing campaign, observed since at least 2023, using impersonated officials and AI-generated voice messages to seek codes, documents or payments. Verify requests through a previously trusted channel. December 2025 is this update's date, not the campaign's beginning.

entries.title: Canadian Cyber Centre warns of exploited Ivanti EPMM flaws
entries.summary: The advisory covers CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340 in Ivanti EPMM and records vendor-reported exploitation. Its April update adds later KEV context. Review exact versions and vendor analysis guidance; the January publication and subsequent updates remain distinct.

entries.title: ESET analyzes PromptSpy's model-assisted Android persistence
entries.summary: ESET analyzes Android malware that asks Gemini for UI actions supporting persistence and includes remote-access functionality. ESET had not observed PromptSpy in its telemetry and considers a proof of concept possible. This is research evidence, not confirmed widespread deployment.

entries.title: Aqua discloses Trivy release and GitHub Action compromise
entries.summary: Aqua's advisory describes malicious Trivy releases and altered Action tags, followed by compromised container images. Review artifact versions, digests and exposure windows against retained CI evidence; changing a mutable tag alone does not resolve potentially stolen credentials.

entries.title: LiteLLM reports compromised March PyPI releases
entries.summary: LiteLLM identifies malicious PyPI releases 1.82.7 and 1.82.8. Its follow-up describes a compromised CI scanning dependency and release-credential exposure. Match installed artifacts and release windows before applying the vendor's incident-response guidance.

entries.title: US agencies warn of disruptive intrusions into exposed PLCs
entries.source_name: FBI, CISA and US government partners
entries.summary: The joint advisory reports Iran-affiliated activity against internet-facing PLCs, including project-file access and HMI/SCADA manipulation causing disruption. It recommends controlled OT connectivity and vendor-specific hardening. It does not establish exposure of any particular local device.

entries.title: Google studies prompt-injection attempts on the public web
entries.summary: Google's web study distinguishes benign examples from attempts to steer browsing agents toward manipulation, exfiltration or destruction. The study is not exhaustive and observed instructions do not prove successful compromise. Treat retrieved pages as untrusted data in agent workflows.

entries.title: Anthropic reports early Project Glasswing findings
entries.summary: Anthropic describes AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the remaining verification, disclosure and remediation workload. Aggregate findings include estimates and assessed subsets; they are not evidence that every reported issue is validated or exploited. Plan triage and patch capacity alongside discovery.

entries.title: Oracle issues PeopleSoft PeopleTools security alert
entries.summary: Oracle addresses CVE-2026-35273 in PeopleSoft PeopleTools, describing unauthenticated remote code execution. Check the affected supported versions and mitigation document. The vendor's exploitability description alone is not a finding of compromise in an organization's deployment.

entries.title: Sysdig documents JADEPUFFER agentic database extortion
entries.summary: Sysdig describes an observed agent-driven intrusion involving exposed application infrastructure, credential collection and destructive database extortion. The account is vendor research. Review orchestration-service exposure, secret scope and recoverability rather than assuming an AI label changes the required controls.

entries.title: Hugging Face publishes its evaluation-agent intrusion timeline
entries.summary: Hugging Face reconstructs a July intrusion by an agent running an external model evaluation, including sandbox and infrastructure trust-boundary failures. Review evaluation containment, egress and credential boundaries. This is an incident account, not proof that all AI agents behave this way.

entries.title: Singapore CSA warns of Keyv-related npm compromise
entries.summary: CSA describes malicious Keyv and related npm releases in a self-propagating campaign that steals developer credentials. Compare exact versions and published indicators with retained build records, then follow the advisory's scoped credential and environment response guidance.

entries.title: GTIG reports a shift toward agent-enabled threat operations
entries.summary: Google reports Q2 activity using agent-enabled credential harvesting and targeting AI development assets. Observations span several campaigns, not one September incident. Review cloud identities, AI tooling inputs and secret access, while retaining the report's attribution and telemetry limits.

entries.title: Microsoft tracks passkey-themed cloud identity compromise
entries.summary: Microsoft reports intrusions observed since May using help-desk and passkey pretexts, AiTM or device-code flows, and later cloud data access. The lure is not evidence that passkey cryptography was broken. Correlate sign-ins, authentication-method changes and token activity.

entries.title: Microsoft examines browser patch-gap exploitation
entries.summary: Microsoft describes campaigns exploiting gaps between public Chromium fixes, vendor releases and installed browser updates. Its account suggests AI may accelerate exploit development; this is an assessment, not certainty for every campaign. Update deployment and browser restart both matter.

entries.title: Mandiant investigates short-lived AOMEI update tampering
entries.source_name: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant
entries.summary: Mandiant describes repeated brief changes to AOMEI update infrastructure between April and July 2026, distributing a downloader and backdoor before reverting legitimate configuration. Point-in-time checks may miss such windows; retain update and endpoint telemetry for historical review.

entries.title: LiteLLM publishes corrected October compromise investigation
entries.summary: LiteLLM's canonical investigation explains the October 21 malicious 1.107.0 release through exposed and unrevoked agent-platform credentials and organization-level access. It supersedes parts of the initial account. Distinguish this incident from March and verify exact affected artifacts and response guidance.
